_meta.what: Safety warnings a pharmacological class declares for its members (class_contexts slugs). Built into `class_warnings`, `class_warning_citations` and `class_warning_exclusions`.
_meta.why: A substance's own binding rows decide most binding-derived warnings, but the long tail of a class has no rows of its own: 37 of 54 phenethylamine psychedelics and 13 of 14 lysergamides carry no 5-HT2B measurement. A class that the literature shows engages the mechanism declares the warning here, and every member shows it.
_meta.declared: One entry per (class, kind). `basis` is the evidence in a sentence, for a curator; the app renders its own localized copy. `citations` are the primary sources for the class claim, at least one. `exclude` names a member that does not inherit the warning, with the reason, so a misfiled member or a subfamily the evidence does not cover stays out without leaving the class.
_meta.not_declared: Classes whose `shared_safety` names the mechanism but which do not declare the warning, each with the reason. The pipeline test requires every class whose shared_safety names 5-HT2B to appear in one of the two lists, so a new class write-up that raises the concern gets a decision rather than silence.

kinds.valvulopathy-5ht2b: Agonism at the 5-HT2B receptor, the mechanism of drug-induced valvular heart disease. The established human association is with chronic or frequent exposure: fenfluramine, the ergot-derived dopamine agonists pergolide and cabergoline, and heavy MDMA use.

declared.basis: MDMA and its active metabolite MDA bind and activate the human 5-HT2B receptor and drive fenfluramine-like mitogenic responses in human valvular interstitial cells (Setola 2003); a later functional assay saw no 5-HT2B activation by MDMA itself but confirmed it for MDA (Rickli 2015, Br J Pharmacol). An echocardiographic case-control study found valvular regurgitation in 8 of 29 MDMA users and none of 29 matched controls (Droogmans 2007).

exclude.reason: An allylbenzene from nutmeg with no amine, filed with the class as a structural precursor. The cited 5-HT2B evidence is for MDMA and MDA, and no 5-HT2B data exist for myristicin.

declared.basis: Most of the benzofurans tested (5-APB, 5-APDB, 6-APB, 6-APDB, 4-APB, 7-APB, 5-EAPB, 5-MAPDB) were partial agonists at the human 5-HT2B receptor, which the authors name as the heart-valve fibrosis risk; the N-dealkylated metabolites 5-APB and 5-APDB are more potent than their parents (Rickli 2015). The mechanism is the one that made fenfluramine and the ergot drugs valvulopathic (Rothman 2000).

exclude.reason: A benzofuran analogue of 5-MeO-DMT rather than an aminopropylbenzofuran. The cited functional data cover the APB/APDB series only.

declared.basis: Every 2C drug and NBOMe derivative tested activated the human 5-HT2B receptor at EC50 below 1 µM, except 2C-H, mescaline and mescaline-NBOMe, and the authors flag cardiac toxicity with chronic use (Rickli 2015). The mechanism is the fenfluramine one (Rothman 2000).

exclude.reason: A mescaline analogue. Mescaline is the exception in the cited assay (5-HT2B EC50 above 1 µM), and escaline's own 5-HT2B row sits below the moderate band.
A mescaline analogue. Mescaline is the exception in the cited assay (5-HT2B EC50 above 1 µM), and its own 5-HT2B row sits below the moderate band.
A mescaline analogue. Mescaline is the exception in the cited assay (5-HT2B EC50 above 1 µM); no proscaline data exist.
A mescaline analogue. Mescaline is the exception in the cited assay (5-HT2B EC50 above 1 µM); no isoproscaline data exist.
A mescaline-type 3,4,5-substituted phenethylamine. Mescaline is the exception in the cited assay (5-HT2B EC50 above 1 µM); no lophophine data exist.
An endogenous µ-opioid peptide, filed in this class by a data error. It has no 5-HT2B activity.

declared.basis: LSD is a partial agonist at the 5-HT2B receptor (Tagen 2023). The ergolines are the class with the strongest human evidence: ergotamine and methysergide's metabolite methylergonovine are 5-HT2B agonists (Rothman 2000), and the ergot-derived dopamine agonists pergolide and cabergoline raised the rate of cardiac-valve regurgitation in a population cohort (Schade 2007).
citations: doi:10.1056/nejmoa062222 Schade 2007, N Engl J Med

declared.basis: Psilocin binds the 5-HT2B receptor with potency equal to or greater than at 5-HT2A and is a partial agonist there; a review of LSD, psilocybin, mescaline, DMT and MDMA judges valvular heart disease a potential risk of chronic microdosing, with no animal or clinical study designed to measure it (Tagen 2023). 4-OH-DiPT activates 5-HT2B below 1 µM (Rickli 2016).

not_declared.reason: The class is heterogeneous at 5-HT2B. Phentermine has no 5-HT2B activity and caused no valvulopathy, while fenfluramine's metabolite norfenfluramine is the archetypal agonist (Rothman 2000). The risk is carried substance by substance, by each member's own binding rows.
The write-up raises the concern for MDMA-like analogues such as 4-MPM only. No 5-HT2B functional data exist for phenmetrazine or its analogues.

The write-up says agonism is 'likely retained by class', which is an inference. No published functional 5-HT2B data exist for 5-IAI, 5-APDI or NM-2-AI; MEAI showed only weak-to-moderate binding (Shimshoni 2018).
The write-up draws the analogy to fenfluramine and MDMA, but no 5-HT2B functional data exist for αMT or αET.
